title: Color coslices of a fibration over inert simplex arrows
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, nerves, full subcategories and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}})$, where inert means the opposite of a consecutive-subinterval inclusion as in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $s:C\to B$ be an inner fibration with $C$ small. Suppose every base arrow has an $s$-cocartesian lift with any prescribed source. Set $A=C_{[1]}$ and regard $A$ as a subcategory of $C$. For $x\in C_{[n]}$ put $J_x=A\times_C C_{x/}$, where $(C_{x/})_r$ consists of $(r+1)$-simplices whose first vertex is $x$, projected to $C$ by the entire remaining face. For each $1\leq i\leq n$, choose an $s$-cocartesian edge $\alpha_i:x\to c_i$ over $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$. Then $A\subset C$ is full and there is a degreewise disjoint-union decomposition
$$J_x=\coprod_{i=1}^n L(x,\rho_i),\qquad L(x,\rho_i)=C_{x/}\times_{B_{[n]/}}\{\rho_i\}.$$
Each summand is a quasicategory with initial object $\alpha_i$; its morphisms retain the commuting triangles and all higher simplices. The decomposition respects target projection to $A$ and the canonical cone from $x$. For $n=0$ the coslice $J_x$ is empty.

external.place: Definition 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.4 and Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.615–616

proof.text: First $B$ and $C$ are quasicategories. Use the nerve and horn conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. An inner horn in the nerve of an ordinary category fills by taking the chain of its consecutive edges and their composites: in dimension two the missing long edge is their composite; in dimension three the required equality of composites is associativity; in higher dimensions each specified face is forced by its consecutive edges. This applies to the inert subcategory, since the composite of $j\mapsto a+j$ and $k\mapsto b+k$ is $k\mapsto a+b+k$, and identities are inert, by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Given an inner horn in $C$, fill its image in $B$ by this chain, and use the inner-fibration lifting property of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] to fill the original horn over that simplex. The same lifting with constant base simplices shows that $A=C\times_B\{[1]\}$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Definitions 3.1.1 and 3.4.1; agent-written nerve and inner-horn calculation for the inert pullback.

proof.text: The inert maps $[n]\to[1]$ are precisely the $\rho_i$, $1\leq i\leq n$: their opposites are $j\mapsto a+j$ on $[1]$, and $0\leq a$, $a+1\leq n$ give $a=i-1$. In particular, the only inert endomorphism of $[1]$ has $a=0$ and is the identity. These are direct substitutions in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. A simplex of $C$ all of whose vertices belong to $A$ therefore maps to a chain in the base all of whose objects are $[1]$ and whose arrows are identities. Its base simplex is constant, so the entire simplex lies in the degreewise fiber $A$. Conversely every simplex of $A$ has those vertices. Thus $A$ is exactly the full subcategory on the objects above $[1]$, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the fiber definition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Definition 3.1.1 (inert maps), supporting unary-fiber calculation for Definition 3.4.1 and Proposition 3.4.5.

proof.text: Unwind the degreewise pullback defining $J_x$, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its $r$-simplices are the maps $\sigma:\Delta^{r+1}\to C$ with first vertex $x$ whose entire remaining face belongs to $A$. The base is therefore a chain $[n]\xrightarrow{f}[1]\xrightarrow{1}[1]\xrightarrow{1}\cdots\xrightarrow{1}[1]$. By step 2, $f$ is a unique $\rho_i$. This is exactly the constant $r$-simplex at the vertex $\rho_i$ in $B_{[n]/}$, so $\sigma$ belongs to the displayed $L(x,\rho_i)$. Conversely an $r$-simplex of this $L$ has constant base on its entire remaining face, so that face lies in $A$ by the fiber definition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and it belongs to $J_x$. These inverse assignments keep the same $\sigma$. Every coslice operator restricts or repeats only the remaining vertices and fixes the first one; it leaves the chain's first base arrow $\rho_i$ unchanged. Thus the degreewise bijections commute with every simplicial operator and give the asserted disjoint-union decomposition, not merely a partition of objects. Distinct $i$ cannot intersect because their base edges differ.

source.place: Supporting calculation for Proposition 3.4.5: agent-written degreewise identification of the unary-target coslice, retaining the full remaining face.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] with $E=C$, $p=s$, $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}})$, the given $x$, and $f=\rho_i$. Its hypotheses require only an inner fibration between quasicategories, verified in step 1. Its displayed lift category is exactly the $L(x,\rho_i)$ of this item: the fixed first vertex, the operators on the remaining vertices, and the constant base vertex all agree. The lemma states that this is a quasicategory and that every cocartesian lift of $\rho_i$ with source $x$ is initial there. The chosen $\alpha_i$ is such a lift by hypothesis; the assumed lift existence ensures these choices are possible. The lemma also states explicitly that morphisms retain the target map over the identity, its commuting triangle and all higher data. This proves initiality in the actual summands, with no discreteness assumption on $A$ or on its mapping spaces.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category dual, as stated by lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality.

proof.text: Both directions of the decomposition in step 3 leave the simplex $\sigma$ unchanged. Consequently the target projection is on each summand the same restriction to its last $r+1$ vertices as the projection $J_x\to A$. The canonical cone from $x$ is encoded by this very $(r+1)$-simplex with its first vertex fixed; restricting or repeating any of its remaining vertices gives the same cone simplex on either side. Hence the identification preserves the canonical cone in every degree, including its triangles and higher coherences. If $n=0$, the inequalities $0\leq a$ and $a+1\leq0$ of step 2 are impossible. A vertex of $J_x$ would give just such a base arrow $[0]\to[1]$, so there are no vertices. Any positive-dimensional simplex has a vertex, hence there are no simplices in any degree. This agrees with the coproduct over the empty index set. All constructions are small because their simplices are subsets of those of the small $C$ in one higher degree.

source.place: Supporting calculation for Proposition 3.4.5: agent-written cone compatibility, smallness and nullary check.

lean.statement: theorem inert_color_coslice_components {C : SSet.{u}} (s : C ⟶ inertSimplexBase.{u}) (hs : cocartesianFibrationOver s) : Subcomplex.range (pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) (inertSimplexVertex 1)) s) = fullSubcomplex C (fun y ↦ s.app (op ⦋0⦌) y = inertSimplexVertex 1) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : C _⦋0⦌) (hx : s.app (op ⦋0⦌) x = inertSimplexVertex n), (∃ e : colorCoslice s x ≅ ∐ (fun i : Fin n ↦ inertColorLiftCategory s x hx i), ∀ (i : Fin n) (r : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (t : (inertColorLiftCategory s x hx i).obj r), colorCosliceSimplex s x (((Sigma.ι (fun j : Fin n ↦ inertColorLiftCategory s x hx j) i) ≫ e.inv).app r t) = inertColorLiftSimplex s x hx i t) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, Quasicategory (inertColorLiftCategory s x hx i) ∧ ∀ α : (inertColorLiftCategory s x hx i) _⦋0⦌, IsCocartesianEdge s (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm (inertColorLiftSimplex s x hx i α)) → IsInitial (inertColorLiftCategory s x hx i) α) ∧ (n = 0 → ∀ r : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, IsEmpty ((colorCoslice s x).obj r))
